messages:
Lina Park: Quick RFC follow-up idea: "minimal seed" that contains a compact, signed manifest + tiny runtime shim + an activation token. The heavy blobs (models, artifact packs) are referenced but not shipped — operator fetches them lazily after seed install. Aim: fit seeds on small USBs and speed initial bring-up for air-gapped installs.

Diego Alvarez: Interesting. How do we avoid a race where operator marks service active but blobs aren't present yet? We saw this cause confusing partial starts in tests.

Radhika Shah: Treat activation as a gated transition. Proposal: states = RECEIVED -> STAGED -> VALIDATED -> ACTIVATED. Only after VALIDATED (all required blob descriptors verified) do we flip an atomic symlink into place. STAGED = unpack + basic checks, VALIDATED = crypto/hash checks + optional fetches.

Tom Becker: I want the operator API to be explicit: POST /seeds/:id/stage, POST /seeds/:id/validate, POST /seeds/:id/activate. Each returns a small activation token or a validation report. That token ties the validate result to the activate call so rollback/duplicate activates are safe.

Lina Park: Exactly. Token should be HMAC(manifest_hash|seed_id|nonce) signed by operator KMS so a replayed validate can't be used against a different manifest. Also include a TTL on validate tokens.

Diego Alvarez: For partial fetches, operator should expose per-blob status: "missing", "verifying", "ok". UI/watchers can subscribe to /seeds/:id/status stream for progress. We'll add a budgeted background fetcher (prefetch_limit) to avoid saturating restricted air-gapped links.

Radhika Shah: Migration: older installers will apply seeds as before -> immediate ACTIVATED. New operator in compatibility mode accepts legacy seeds and treats them as STAGED+VALIDATED automatically (best-effort). We'll gate by operator version header and a feature toggle.

Tom Becker: Edge case: media resume on different node. Seed metadata must include seed_uuid + manifest_hash + sequence number. If node receives a seed with same seed_uuid but different manifest_hash, operator rejects unless explicit admin override. If same manifest_hash and status ACTIVATED, apply should be noop.

Lina Park: Observability: emit structured events for each transition (seed.received, seed.staged, seed.validated, seed.activated) with metadata (manifest_hash, missing_count, duration). This makes debugging power-cut/resume flows easier.

Diego Alvarez: Security: manifest references include {blob_id, length, sha256, sig, compression}. Operator verifies sigs and rejects mismatches. Consider optional attestation from media vendor but don't require for first pass.

Radhika Shah: Tests: add chaos-suite scenarios: mid-transfer power loss, interrupted verify then resume on different host, and partial blob corruption. Also create a tiny "simulate-limited-link" e2e test that throttles fetcher and asserts operator stays in STAGED/VALIDATING until complete.

Tom Becker: Quick example API flow:
```
# stage
curl -X POST -H "Operator-Version: v2" /seeds/abc123/stage -d @seed.tar
# validate -> returns token
curl -X POST /seeds/abc123/validate -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"mode":"strict"}'
# activate
curl -X POST /seeds/abc123/activate -H "X-Validate-Token: <token>"
```

Lina Park: I'll draft a short RFC with diagrams, the state machine semantics, operator endpoints, token format, and a compat + rollout plan (canary operators, feature flag on installers). Meeting Friday 11am to review? :calendar:  

Diego Alvarez: +1, will bring failure-mode test cases. :thumbsup:

Radhika Shah: I'll write the KMS/HSM integration section and a simple threat model (replay, forged media, partial inject).

ops-bot: Reminder: add new seed transition metrics to the operator telemetry dashboard.
